claims.statement: A tag turn's prompt has a fixed five-part shape: the system prompt is the audience's `Doctrine.text`, followed by a `<context_header>` user message, then one user message led by the clock line and every assembled block in `order`, then the assistant `CLOSING_LINE`, and finally `build_tag_message`'s output handed to the agent as the invocation prompt.

`BlockKey` records what a block's content varies by (`global`/`unit`/`room`/`person`/`turn`) and therefore, structurally, how many distinct prompt prefixes the block creates: a value keyed narrower than `global` cannot sit in a byte-identical head, so every row is served in the per-turn message, the field defaults to `turn` as the safe end, and `test_no_block_in_this_table_belongs_in_the_cached_head` asserts no built block is keyed `global`. The asymmetry is why the declaration matters: a block wrongly declared `turn` costs only the prefix it never had, while one wrongly declared `global` ends the prefix match in every room where its value differs, whatever its rewrite interval.

`nora/agent/prefill.py`'s `_BLOCKS` declares the tag path's blocks once as name/order/scope-key rows; `_ROW` derives the lookup and `_block` fills a block's `order` and `key` from the table, so a block cannot be served without a row and a table row cannot be served without a renderer.

`restamp` stamps a block built in another package with this prompt's `order` and `key` and nothing else, raising `KeyError` for a name the caller never declared, so the block's identity, content and description stay owned by its own module while its placement stays owned by the prompt.

`_declared` emits an empty stub for every declared block that rendered nothing, so the `agent.prefill` span reports `blocks_declared`, `blocks_rendered`, `blocks_empty` and `size_chars` and a silently failing read is distinguishable from a genuinely empty one.

`assemble` treats block order as data, sorting by `order`, and drops any block whose body is empty unless the block opts out through `when_empty`; with no separator each block is followed by one newline, and with a separator the blocks are joined so nothing trails the last one.

Every block type is declared once in `BLOCK_TYPES` as `BlockType(name, description, annotations)`, and `ContextBlock.description`/`annotation` are read-only properties looked up by name, so a renderer selects a description instead of composing one and an unknown name raises at construction rather than at render, where `assemble` would have dropped an empty body first.

`ContextBlock.__post_init__` refuses `description`/`fields` in `attrs` and refuses attribute names outside `[A-Za-z_][\w.-]*`, because `render()` writes caller attributes before the derived pair and writes keys raw — otherwise a caller could emit a second `description=` on one element that most readers would take as the block's own.

There is no block catalogue and no `untrusted` marker: what a block is and what its fields mean travel in the block's own opening tag as `description=` and `fields=`, and a type-level annotation may not name a tool because the relevance gate renders the same type and holds no tools.

Escaping is unconditional in the shared renderers: `escape` closes the tag boundary, `escape_attr` also closes the quoted attribute, `one_line` closes the line boundary, and none is a switchable `RowStyle` field — `render_messages` instead puts each record in its own element so a body keeps its line breaks while a forged closing tag is unwritable.

Authored text around the blocks (situation paragraphs, fire headers, the clock line, the closing line, the summons' head) lives in `nora/domain/framing.py` as one frozen dataclass builder per piece, where every person- or store-controlled value enters through `_put` marked `escaped`, `carried`, `joined` or `system`, and `_put` is the only function there that calls `escape`.

Doctrine `kind` splits authored files (`constraint`, `identity`, `conduct`, `instrument`) from the single derived kind (`situation`); a file claiming `situation` is refused, and the same `kind` both gates the file during the scan and is rendered into `<section kind=...>` so the label the model reads is the rule that was enforced.

`applies_to` is a closed vocabulary of the nine consuming audiences plus `always`, and an unknown name is refused at parse, because `get()` filters sections by string membership and a typo would silently remove a file from every prompt while the reload-failure counter stayed flat.

`authority_above`/`authority_below` are checked as a strict partial order over doctrine sections — every name must resolve to a section or one of the authority terminals, both declarations of an edge must agree, and the relation must be acyclic — with unranked peers allowed inside a tier rather than an order invented between files nothing reads at inference time.

`[doctrine] reload` selects the lifecycle: `mtime` re-fingerprints every file's path, `st_mtime_ns` and size on each read and rescans when the fingerprint moves, so an edit is live on the next turn with no rebuild, while `startup` freezes the corpus after the first successful scan; size is in the fingerprint because an edit restored at its original timestamp moves no clock and would otherwise serve old text silently.

A doctrine rescan that fails after a good load keeps serving the previous sections, increments `nora_doctrine_reload_failures_total`, logs one `doctrine_reload_failed` line and advances the fingerprint, while a failed first scan raises so a process cannot start with no instructions; only a successful scan bumps `generation`, which is the only thing that clears the per-audience assembly cache.

`DoctrineSection.sha256` is taken over `render_section` — the served bytes, `description` included — so `tests/test_doctrine_version_parity.py` can refuse a served edit that reaches `master` without a version bump, but it is a repo gate rather than a runtime guard: an operator editing the corpus on the deploy host is not stopped by it.

The relevance gate carries its own two-row `_BLOCKS` (`group_transcript` at order 10, `standing` at order 20, both keyed `turn`) and renders them through `ContextBlock` and `assemble` rather than the tag prefill assembler, so its input stays a closed set; it renders `<standing>` as `(none)` rather than nothing because `assemble` would drop an empty body along with the sentence explaining that absence.

Because a scan that succeeds with a missing or empty `participation.md` is not a reload failure, the relevance gate refuses to send when its audience resolves to zero sections or an empty body, failing closed rather than reporting as a working gate with no criteria.

ADR 0021's rule is enforced by discovery: `tests/architecture/test_every_model_call_is_a_declared_occasion.py` reads `nora/` source, finds every module that calls a model by a known door or defines `inputs`, and requires a non-empty module-level `_BLOCKS` plus a call to the `assemble` imported from `nora.domain.blocks`; a hand `.join` of `.render()` results is a violation even beside a working `assemble`.

Modules that run or transport a prompt another module builds are classified rather than recorded as debt — MECHANISM, RUNNER (naming its builders and how they are reached) and EXEMPT (an authored prompt plus media) — each with a written reason the test re-checks, and there is no PENDING ledger, `CEILING` or per-occasion exception.

The typed-block gate checks both directions — every rendered block name has a declared type and every declared type is rendered — and adds population-wide checks: a description must be a sentence rather than a label, may not lean on internal vocabulary such as `tier` or `injector`, and a sentence discussing absence must carry the R-27 hedge in that same sentence.

`test_one_block_injector` keeps modules from opening and closing a model-facing element by hand: a discovered hand-written tag must either be routed through `ContextBlock` or classified with a written reason, and a classification whose module no longer writes a tag fails as stale.

The tag path and the fire path share one renderer: `TranscriptInjection.assemble` and `FirePath.build_context` each build a `TagContext` and both hand it to `build_prefill`, which differs between them only in the situation paragraph passed as `header`; `build_assembler` is the single construction site for `TranscriptInjection`, pinned by `test_assembler_parity`.

With `[persona] render` on, the seven rows in `_PERSONA_REPLACES` are not rendered, their stubs leave the declared list, and `<persona>` blocks are stamped into those same orders, so the prompt's read order survives the cutover.

The prefill order widens from her own account through the people, the unit's notes and decisions and the room's culture, then breaks scope on purpose: `standing` at 60 and `standing_working_set` at 65 sit immediately before `group_transcript` at 70 so the pair reads as where she had got to and what has been said since.

Assembly owns the static head's byte-identity rather than any measured saving: `<context_header>` carries nothing that changes between tags and the clock leads the volatile block instead, so the head is eligible for a prefix-cache hit, while whether a serving route charges less for the repeated prefix is a property of the provider and model to be re-measured there.

`<tool_catalogue>` renders only when tools are deferred (`[llm] defer_tools`, off by default): `ToolSurface.prompt_catalogue` returns the index only when something is on the shelf and an empty string when every admitted tool is already resident, so the block cannot become a second copy of schemas the request already carries.
